entities.name: Caroline
entities.description: A transgender woman who moved from Sweden around 2019 and began transitioning around 2020. She paints, draws and makes stained glass, plays acoustic guitar and was learning the piano in July 2023, and is pursuing a career in counselling and mental health. Through 2023 she attended an LGBTQ support group, spoke at a school, mentored an LGBTQ teenager, joined the activist group Connected LGBTQ Activists and volunteered at an LGBTQ+ youth centre, while working towards adopting a child as a single parent. She is Melanie's friend and one of the two speakers in this conversation.

entities.name: Melanie
entities.description: A married mother of at least three children and the other speaker in this conversation. She paints landscapes, still life and animals, took up pottery in July 2023, runs to de-stress, plays the violin and the clarinet, and camps with her family every summer. She was married around 2018, ran a mental-health charity race in May 2023, and was injured in September 2023 which forced a break from pottery.

entities.name: Melanie's husband
entities.description: Melanie's husband and the father of her children, never named in the conversation and referred to as 'my husband' and 'my partner'. They married around 2018 in a ceremony Melanie remembers as full of love, and he is one of the people who keep her motivated.

entities.name: Melanie's children
entities.description: The group of Melanie's children, referred to throughout as 'the kids' and never named individually. There are at least three: a son who was in a car accident on the October 2023 road trip, a daughter whose birthday was celebrated at a concert on 13 August 2023, and a youngest daughter whose first steps Melanie remembers. Two of them are described as the younger ones who love nature. They go camping, hiking, to the beach and to museums with their parents, and paint and make pottery with their mother.

properties.aliases: the kids, my fam, my little ones

entities.name: Caroline's friends, family and mentors
entities.description: The group of people Caroline calls her rocks — the friends she has known for four years since moving from Sweden, her family, and her mentors. They supported her through her transition and a tough breakup, meet up with her, had a picnic with her in early July 2023, and are who she credits with helping her find out who she is. One of the mentors advised her on adoption in October 2023.

properties.aliases: my friends, family and mentors, my support system, my rocks

entities.name: Caroline's mentee
entities.description: A transgender teenager Caroline mentors through the LGBTQ youth mentorship program she joined in July 2023. They work together on building confidence and positive strategies, and went to an LGBT pride event together in June 2023, where Caroline's best moment was seeing the teenager's face light up at the support around them.

properties.aliases: a transgender teen just like me, my mentee

entities.name: Caroline's grandmother
entities.description: Caroline's grandmother in Sweden, who gave her the cross-and-heart necklace when she was young as a symbol of love, faith and strength.

entities.name: Caroline's father
entities.description: Caroline's dad, who took her horseback riding through the fields when she was a child — the source of her lasting love of horses.

entities.name: Amy Ellis Nutt
entities.description: The author of 'Becoming Nicole', the book Caroline names as her favourite guide.

entities.name: Sara Bareilles
entities.description: The singer of 'Brave', the song Caroline says has a lot of significance for her.

entities.name: Matt Patterson
entities.description: The musician whose concert Melanie and her family attended on 13 August 2023 for her daughter's birthday; Melanie thought his voice and songs were amazing.

entities.name: Oscar
entities.description: Caroline's guinea pig, whose favourite food is parsley. Caroline introduced him on 23 August 2023 when Melanie asked whether she had any pets.

entities.name: Luna
entities.description: Melanie's cat, one of the household's pets alongside the dog Oliver; a second cat, Bailey, joined them by August 2023.

entities.name: Oliver
entities.description: Melanie's black dog. The funniest thing he has done, she says, was hiding his bone in her slipper.

entities.name: Bailey
entities.description: The second cat Melanie's household acquired, first mentioned on 23 August 2023 alongside Luna and Oliver.

entities.name: Sweden
entities.description: Caroline's home country, which she left around 2019. Her grandmother, who gave her the necklace she treasures, lives there.

entities.name: the Grand Canyon
entities.description: The destination of Melanie's family road trip over the weekend of 14–15 October 2023; her children enjoyed it despite the car accident that began the trip.

entities.name: Caroline's LGBTQ support group
entities.description: The LGBTQ support group Caroline attended on 7 May 2023, where transgender people's stories inspired her. She says it has made her feel accepted and given her the courage to embrace herself, and it is part of why she wants to work in counselling.

entities.name: Connected LGBTQ Activists
entities.description: The LGBTQ activist group Caroline joined on 18 July 2023. Its members come from all walks of life, and it holds regular meetings and plans events and campaigns for rights and community support.

entities.name: the LGBTQ+ youth centre
entities.description: The LGBTQ+ youth centre where Caroline volunteers, talking to young people and sharing her own story so they know they are not alone. She intends to keep volunteering there and was helping put on a talent show for the young people in September 2023. Read here as the same place as the 'LGBTQ center' she visited in July 2023 before painting her art-show piece, which the conversation neither confirms nor rules out.

entities.name: the LGBTQ youth mentorship program
entities.description: The mentorship program for LGBTQ youth that Caroline joined over the weekend of 15–16 July 2023, through which she mentors a transgender teenager. Kept separate from the LGBTQ+ youth centre she volunteers at, because the conversation never says the two are the same.

entities.name: Melanie's pottery class
entities.description: The pottery class Melanie signed up for on 2 July 2023. She made a black-and-white flower bowl, a colourful bowl and a flower-decorated plate in it, and stopped attending for a while after being hurt in September 2023.

entities.name: the LGBTQ-friendly adoption agency
entities.description: The adoption agency Caroline picked out in May 2023 because it helps LGBTQ+ people adopt; its inclusivity and support spoke to her. She applied in August 2023 and passed its interviews on 20 October 2023.

entities.name: Summer Sounds
entities.description: The band Melanie saw play live; they played a pop song that got the whole crowd dancing and singing. She described the gig on 28 August 2023.

entities.name: Becoming Nicole
entities.description: Amy Ellis Nutt's true story of a trans girl and her family. Caroline's favourite book and the one she recommends: it made her feel connected, gave her hope for her own path and taught her self-acceptance and how to find support.

entities.name: Charlotte's Web
entities.description: Melanie's favourite book from her childhood, which showed her how friendship and compassion can make a difference.

entities.name: Brave
entities.description: Sara Bareilles's song about being courageous and fighting for what is right. Caroline says it has a lot of significance for her and makes her think about the paths she has taken and the progress she has made.

entities.name: Perfect
entities.description: Ed Sheeran's song, named by Melanie as the modern music she likes alongside classical composers such as Bach and Mozart.

entities.name: Embracing Identity
entities.description: Caroline's painting of a woman, shown to Melanie on 14 August 2023. It is about finding comfort and love in being yourself; the woman stands for the journey of acceptance, and Caroline meant it to convey warmth, love and self-acceptance.

entities.name: Caroline's stained glass window for a local church
entities.description: A stained glass window Caroline made for a local church, described on 25 August 2023. It shows time changing our lives, stands for her own journey as a transgender woman and for accepting growth and change, and is meant to remind people that the key to their true potential is within them.

entities.name: Caroline's cross-and-heart necklace
entities.description: A necklace with a cross and a heart that Caroline's grandmother in Sweden gave her when she was young. It stands for love, faith and strength and reminds her of her roots and her family's support.

entities.name: Caroline's hand-painted bowl
entities.description: A hand-painted bowl a friend made for Caroline's 18th birthday, about ten years before June 2023. She treasures its pattern and colours as a reminder of art and self-expression.

entities.name: painting
entities.description: The art both women make. Melanie has painted for about seven years — landscapes, still life, animals, sunsets and abstracts, often together with her children — and Caroline has made art since she was about 17, painting her trans experience, self-portraits, sunsets, flowers and abstracts, and showing them at an LGBTQ art show she is organising.

entities.name: pottery
entities.description: Melanie's second art form, taken up in July 2023. She calls it a huge part of her life rather than a hobby: it is calming, it lets her express her emotions, and she has made bowls and a plate in her class and taken her children to a workshop. Caroline had still not tried it by September 2023 but said she was game to.

entities.name: running
entities.description: Melanie's way of de-stressing and clearing her mind. It is part of the daily me-time she carved out from May 2023, she ran a mental-health charity race on 20 May 2023, and by July 2023 she was running longer distances and says it has improved her mental health.

entities.name: Melanie's family camping trips
entities.description: The camping Melanie does with her husband and children — in the mountains, in forests and at the beach — which she calls the highlight of their summer and a family tradition. They roast marshmallows, tell stories round the campfire and hike, and her best memory is watching the Perseid meteor shower on their 2022 trip.

entities.name: Caroline's adoption
entities.description: Caroline's undertaking to adopt a child as a single parent, which she calls a lifelong dream. It ran from researching agencies in May 2023, through picking an LGBTQ-friendly agency, attending an adoption council meeting on 14 July 2023 and an adoption advice group, applying to agencies in the week of 23 August 2023 and asking a mentor for advice on 13 October 2023, to passing the agency interviews on 20 October 2023. She is also building a children's library ready for it.

entities.name: Caroline's move into counselling and mental health
entities.description: Caroline's plan to continue her education and build a career in counselling or mental health work, first mentioned on 8 May 2023 and returned to in most sessions through July 2023. She wants to work with trans people on self-acceptance and mental health, because counselling and support groups helped her through her own struggles, and she attended an LGBTQ+ counselling workshop on 23 June 2023 as part of it.

entities.name: Caroline's gender transition
entities.description: Caroline's transition as a transgender woman, begun about three years before June 2023. She speaks about it publicly — at a school event, at conferences and through her art — and says her friends, family and mentors were instrumental in it; some close friends could not handle it and the relationships that remain feel more genuine to her.

entities.name: Caroline's LGBTQ art show
entities.description: An art show of LGBTQ artists that Caroline is putting together and will show her paintings at. On 17 July 2023 she said it was happening the following month; by 25 August 2023 she described it as next month again, making it September 2023. She painted a tree with a bright sun behind it for it, and means it to spread understanding and acceptance.

claims.text: Caroline's art is about expressing her trans experience: showing her story and helping people understand the trans community.

claims.text: Caroline's painting 'Embracing Identity' is about finding comfort and love in being yourself; the woman in it stands for the journey of acceptance, and Caroline meant it to show warmth, love and self-acceptance.
